docs.title: Getting Started with FreeStack
docs.text: This guide will help you get FreeStack up and running quickly.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+
  • PostgreSQL 15+
  • Redis 7+
  • (Optional) Docker & Docker Compose

docs.title: Quick Start (Docker)
docs.text:
The fastest way to get started is using Docker Compose:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/yourorg/freestack.git
cd freestack

# Copy example config
cp config.example.yaml config.yaml

# Start all services
docker-compose up -d

# Run migrations
docker-compose exec api freestack db upgrade

# Seed development data (optional)
docker-compose exec api freestack db seed

The API will be available at: - API: http://localhost:8000 - Docs: http://localhost:8000/docs - Health: http://localhost:8000/health - WebSocket: ws://localhost:8001

docs.title: 1. Set up Python environment
docs.text:
# Using uv (recommended)
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
uv pip install -e .

# Or using standard venv
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
pip install -e .

docs.title: 2. Configure environment
docs.text:
cp config.example.yaml config.yaml
# Edit config.yaml with your settings

Required settings: - database.url - PostgreSQL connection string - redis.url - Redis connection string - auth.secret_key - Generate with freestack generate secret

docs.title: 3. Start dependencies
docs.text:
# Using Docker for just dependencies
docker-compose up -d postgres redis

# Or install locally
# PostgreSQL: https://www.postgresql.org/download/
# Redis: https://redis.io/download/

docs.title: 4. Run migrations
docs.text: freestack db upgrade

docs.title: 5. Seed development data (optional)
docs.text:
freestack db seed

This creates: - Admin user: admin@freestack.local / admin123 - Test user: user@freestack.local / user123

docs.title: 6. Start the API server
docs.text: freestack api serve --reload

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
# Health check
curl http://localhost:8000/health

# API info
curl http://localhost:8000/info

# Login
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "admin@freestack.local", "password": "admin123"}'

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: FreeStack follows a modular, layered architecture designed for scalability, maintainability, and developer experience.

docs.title: 1. Separation of Concerns
docs.text: Each layer has a single responsibility: - Core: Shared infrastructure (config, DB, auth, logging, events) - Models: Data models and schemas (SQLAlchemy + Pydantic) - API: HTTP layer (FastAPI, routing, middleware) - CLI: Command-line interface (Typer, Rich) - Services: Background processing (workers, scheduler, WebSocket)

docs.title: 2. Dependency Injection
docs.text: FastAPI's dependency injection system is used throughout for: - Database sessions - Authentication - Configuration - External services

docs.title: 3. Async-First
docs.text: All I/O operations use async/await: - Database: SQLAlchemy 2.0 async - HTTP: httpx, FastAPI - Redis: redis-py async - WebSockets: websockets library

docs.title: 4. Type Safety
docs.text: Full type annotations with: - Pydantic for validation - SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed models - mypy for static checking - py.typed marker for library consumers

docs.title: 5. Configuration as Code
docs.text: Layered configuration with validation: 1. Default values (code) 2. YAML config file 3. Environment variables 4. CLI arguments

docs.title: Configuration (core/config.py)
docs.text:
• Pydantic Settings with nested models
  • Environment variable support with FREESTACK_ prefix
  • YAML file loading with layered overrides
  • Type validation and defaults

docs.title: Database (core/database.py)
docs.text:
• SQLAlchemy 2.0 async engine/session
  • Connection pooling with health checks
  • Repository pattern for data access
  • Alembic migrations

docs.title: Authentication (core/auth.py)
docs.text:
• JWT tokens (access + refresh)
  • bcrypt password hashing
  • Role-based access control (RBAC)
  • Permission system with hierarchy

docs.title: Events (core/events.py)
docs.text:
• Typed event bus (sync + async handlers)
  • Middleware support
  • Outbox pattern for reliability
  • Event store for event sourcing

docs.title: Health Checks (core/health.py)
docs.text:
• Liveness probe (basic)
  • Readiness probe (critical deps)
  • Extensible check framework
  • Prometheus metrics integration

docs.title: Request Flow (API)
docs.text:
Client Request
     │
     ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Middleware     │  ← Correlation ID, Logging, Security Headers, Rate Limit
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Router         │  ← FastAPI routing, validation
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Dependencies   │  ← DB session, Auth, Pagination
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Handler        │  ← Business logic
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Response       │  ← Pydantic serialization
└─────────────────┘

docs.title: Background Job Flow
docs.text:
Enqueue Job
     │
     ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Redis Queue    │  ← Arq job queue
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Worker         │  ← Concurrency control, retries
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Job Handler    │  ← Business logic
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│  Result/Events  │  ← Store result, emit events
└─────────────────┘

docs.title: Defense in Depth
docs.text:
1. Network: Private networks, load balancers, WAF
  2. Transport: TLS 1.3, HSTS, secure headers
  3. Application: Input validation, rate limiting, CORS
  4. Authentication: JWT, API keys, OAuth2/OIDC
  5. Authorization: RBAC, resource-level permissions
  6. Data: Encryption at rest, field-level encryption
  7. Audit: Comprehensive audit logging

docs.title: Secrets Management
docs.text:
• Never commit secrets to version control
  • Use environment variables or secret managers
  • Rotate secrets regularly
  • Audit secret access

docs.title: Horizontal Scaling
docs.text:
• Stateless API servers (add more workers)
  • Redis for session/cache sharing
  • Database connection pooling
  • Read replicas for queries

docs.title: Caching Strategy
docs.text:
• Redis for distributed caching
  • HTTP caching headers
  • Query result caching
  • Template fragment caching

docs.title: Database Optimization
docs.text:
• Connection pooling (PgBouncer)
  • Read replicas
  • Partitioning for large tables
  • Proper indexing

docs.title: Metrics (Prometheus)
docs.text:
• HTTP request rate, latency, errors
  • Database query performance
  • Queue depth, job duration
  • Business metrics

docs.title: Logging (Structured JSON)
docs.text:
• Correlation IDs for request tracing
  • Structured fields for querying
  • Log levels: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR
  • Centralized log aggregation

docs.title: Tracing (OpenTelemetry)
docs.text:

  • Integration with Jaeger/Zipkin

docs.title: Health Checks
docs.text:
• Liveness: Process is running
  • Readiness: Dependencies available
  • Startup: Initialization complete

docs.title: FreeStack Configuration Guide
docs.text: Complete reference for all configuration options.

docs.title: Configuration Layers
docs.text: FreeStack uses layered configuration (highest priority first): 1. CLI arguments 2. Environment variables (FREESTACK_ prefix) 3. config.yaml file 4. Default values

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
Create config.yaml from config.example.yaml:

cp config.example.yaml config.yaml

docs.title: Application
docs.text:
app:
  name: "freestack"              # Application name
  environment: "development"     # development | staging | production
  debug: true                    # Enable debug mode
  timezone: "UTC"                # Application timezone

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
database:
  url: "postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@host:5432/db"
  pool_size: 20                  # Connection pool size
  max_overflow: 10               # Extra connections above pool_size
  pool_timeout: 30               # Seconds to wait for connection
  pool_recycle: 3600             # Recycle connections (seconds)
  pool_pre_ping: true            # Verify connections before use
  echo: false                    # Log SQL queries
  echo_pool: false               # Log pool events

docs.title: Redis
docs.text:
redis:
  url: "redis://host:6379/0"
  max_connections: 50
  socket_timeout: 5
  socket_connect_timeout: 5
  retry_on_timeout: true
  health_check_interval: 30

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
auth:
  secret_key: "your-secret-key"  # REQUIRED - 32+ bytes for production
  algorithm: "HS256"             # JWT algorithm
  access_token_expire_minutes: 30
  refresh_token_expire_days: 7
  password_min_length: 12
  password_require_uppercase: true
  password_require_lowercase: true
  password_require_numbers: true
  password_require_symbols: true
  bcrypt_rounds: 12

docs.title: API Server
docs.text:
api:
  host: "0.0.0.0"
  port: 8000
  workers: 4                     # Gunicorn workers
  worker_class: "uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker"
  cors_origins:
    - "http://localhost:3000"
  cors_allow_credentials: true
  cors_allow_methods:
    - "GET"
    - "POST"
    - "PUT"
    - "PATCH"
    - "DELETE"
    - "OPTIONS"
  cors_allow_headers:
    - "*"
  rate_limit: "100/minute"
  rate_limit_storage: "redis"
  request_timeout: 30
  max_request_size: 10485760
  docs_url: "/docs"
  redoc_url: "/redoc"
  openapi_url: "/openapi.json"

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
cli:
  theme: "dark"                  # dark | light
  show_progress: true
  confirm_destructive: true
  history_file: "~/.freestack_history"
  completion: true

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
logging:
  level: "INFO"                  # DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR
  format: "json"                 # json | console
  file: "logs/app.log"
  max_bytes: 10485760            # 10MB
  backup_count: 5
  encoding: "utf-8"
  include_timestamp: true
  include_level: true
  include_logger: true
  include_module: true
  include_function: true
  include_line: true

docs.title: Background Worker
docs.text:
worker:
  concurrency: 4
  max_jobs: 1000
  job_timeout: 300
  retry_attempts: 3
  retry_backoff: 60
  dead_letter_queue: true
  queues:
    - "default"
    - "high"
    - "low"

docs.title: Scheduler
docs.text:
scheduler:
  enabled: true
  timezone: "UTC"
  max_instances: 3
  coalesce: true
  misfire_grace_time: 30

docs.title: WebSocket
docs.text:
websocket:
  host: "0.0.0.0"
  port: 8001
  ping_interval: 20
  ping_timeout: 10
  max_message_size: 1048576
  max_connections: 10000

docs.title: File Storage

docs.title: Security Headers
docs.text:
security:
  headers:
    x_content_type_options: "nosniff"
    x_frame_options: "DENY"
    x_xss_protection: "1; mode=block"
    strict_transport_security: "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
    content_security_policy: "default-src 'self'"
    referrer_policy: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    permissions_policy: "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()"
  cors:
    allow_origins: []
    allow_methods: []
    allow_headers: []
    allow_credentials: false
    max_age: 600

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
All settings can be overridden with environment variables using the FREESTACK_ prefix and double underscores for nesting:

# Application
FREESTACK_APP__ENVIRONMENT=production
FREESTACK_APP__DEBUG=false

# Database
FREESTACK_DATABASE__URL=postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@host:5432/db

# Redis
FREESTACK_REDIS__URL=redis://host:6379/0

# Auth
FREESTACK_AUTH__SECRET_KEY=your-secret-key
FREESTACK_AUTH__ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES=30

# API
FREESTACK_API__HOST=0.0.0.0
FREESTACK_API__PORT=8000
FREESTACK_API__WORKERS=4
FREESTACK_API__CORS_ORIGINS=https://app.example.com
FREESTACK_API__RATE_LIMIT=200/minute

# Logging
FREESTACK_LOGGING__LEVEL=INFO
FREESTACK_LOGGING__FORMAT=json

# Worker
FREESTACK_WORKER__CONCURRENCY=8

docs.title: Never Commit Secrets
docs.text:
• Add config.yaml to .gitignore
  • Use environment variables in production
  • Use secret managers (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, etc.)

docs.title: Generating Secret Key
docs.text:
# Using CLI
freestack generate secret

# Using Python
python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"

# Using OpenSSL
openssl rand -hex 32

docs.text:
# docker-compose.yml

    secrets:
      - secret_key

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Configuration is validated on startup. Invalid config will cause the application to fail fast with clear error messages.

Run validation manually: 

freestack config validate

docs.title: FreeStack Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide covers deploying FreeStack to production environments.

docs.title: Docker Compose (Single Server)
docs.text:
Best for small deployments, staging, or development.

# Build image
docker build -t freestack:latest .

# Create environment file
cp .env.example .env.production
# Edit .env.production with production values

# Deploy
docker-compose --env-file .env.production up -d

docs.title: Kubernetes (Helm)
docs.text:
Best for production with scaling, self-healing, and rolling updates.

# Add Helm repo
helm repo add freestack https://charts.freestack.dev

# Install
helm install freestack freestack/freestack \
  --namespace freestack \
  --create-namespace \
  --set database.url=postgresql://... \
  --set redis.url=redis://... \
  --set auth.secretKey=...

docs.title: Manual Deployment
docs.text:
For custom infrastructure.

# Build
docker build -t freestack:latest .

# Run
docker run -d \
  --name freestack-api \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -e FREESTACK_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... \
  -e FREESTACK_REDIS_URL=redis://... \
  -e FREESTACK_SECRET_KEY=... \
  -e FREESTACK_ENVIRONMENT=production \
  freestack:latest

docs.title: Docker Compose Production Override
docs.text:
Create docker-compose.prod.yml:

version: '3.8'

services:
  api:
    image: freestack:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '2'
          memory: 2G
        reservations:
          cpus: '1'
          memory: 1G
      restart_policy:
        condition: on-failure
        delay: 5s
        max_attempts: 3
    logging:
      driver: "json-file"
      options:
        max-size: "10m"
        max-file: "3"

  worker:
    image: freestack:latest
    command: freestack worker start --concurrency 8
    deploy:
      replicas: 2

  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./config/nginx/prod.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./certs:/etc/nginx/certs:ro
    depends_on:
      - api

Deploy with: 

docker-compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env.production up -d

    spec:
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: freestack:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8000
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: freestack-config
        - secretRef:
            name: freestack-secrets
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "512Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
          limits:
            memory: "2Gi"
            cpu: "2000m"
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8000
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health/ready
            port: 8000
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 5

docs.title: Database Scaling
docs.text:
• Read replicas for SELECT queries
  • Connection pooling (PgBouncer)
  • Partitioning for large tables
  • Consider read models for complex queries

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Database connection failures - Check network connectivity - Verify credentials - Check connection pool settings - Monitor PostgreSQL logs

Redis connection failures - Check Redis is running - Verify URL and credentials - Check memory limits - Monitor Redis logs

High latency - Check database query performance - Enable query logging - Add indexes - Check for N+1 queries

Memory issues - Check for memory leaks - Monitor worker memory - Adjust worker concurrency - Profile with py-spy

docs.title: FreeStack Development Guide
docs.text: This guide covers setting up and working with the FreeStack codebase.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+
  • PostgreSQL 15+
  • Redis 7+
  • Git
  • (Optional) Docker & Docker Compose

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
# Clone
git clone https://github.com/yourorg/freestack.git
cd freestack

# Run setup script
./scripts/dev-setup.sh

# Or manual setup:
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
pip install -e .
pre-commit install
cp config.example.yaml config.yaml

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Edit config.yaml for local development:

app:
  environment: "development"
  debug: true

database:
  url: "postgresql+asyncpg://freestack:freestack@localhost:5432/freestack"

redis:
  url: "redis://localhost:6379/0"

auth:
  secret_key: "dev-secret-key-change-in-production"

docs.title: Start Dependencies
docs.text:
# With Docker (recommended)
docker-compose up -d postgres redis

# Or install locally

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
freestack/
├── core/           # Core framework (config, DB, auth, events, health)

docs.title: Python Style
docs.text:
• Formatter: Black (line length 100)
  • Linter: Ruff (with all rules enabled)
  • Imports: isort (Black profile)
  • Types: mypy (strict mode)

docs.title: Type Hints
docs.text:
• All functions must have type hints
  • Use from __future__ import annotations
  • Prefer list[str] over List[str] (Python 3.9+)
  • Use TypedDict for dict schemas

docs.title: Async Patterns
docs.text:
• Use async/await for all I/O
  • Avoid blocking calls in async functions
  • Use asyncio.gather for parallel operations
  • Use async with for context managers

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Use custom exceptions for domain errors
  • Log errors with structured logging
  • Return appropriate HTTP status codes
  • Don't leak internal details in responses

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Unit tests for business logic
  • Integration tests for API endpoints
  • Use fixtures for common setup
  • Mock external services
  • Aim for >80% coverage

docs.title: Adding a New Model
docs.text:
1. Create model in models/: 

    # models/item.py
from sqlalchemy import String, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship
from .base import Base, IDMixin, TimestampMixin

class Item(Base, IDMixin, TimestampMixin):
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(100), nullable=False)
    description: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(500), nullable=True)
    owner_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("users.id"), nullable=False)
    owner: Mapped["User"] = relationship("User", back_populates="items")

  2. Add to models/__init__.py

  3. Create migration: 

    freestack db revision -m "Add Item model"

  4. Create Pydantic schemas in same file

docs.title: Adding a New API Endpoint
docs.text:
1. Create route module in api/routes/: 

    # api/routes/items.py
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from ...core.database import get_db
from ...api.dependencies import get_current_active_user
from ...models.item import Item, ItemCreate, ItemResponse

router = APIRouter(prefix="/items", tags=["items"])

@router.post("", response_model=ItemResponse)
async def create_item(
    item_data: ItemCreate,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_active_user),
):
    # Implementation
    pass

  2. Register in api/main.py: 

    from .routes import items
app.include_router(items.router)

docs.text:

JOBS["process_item"] = process_item_job

    from services.worker import enqueue_job_async

job_id = await enqueue_job_async("process_item", item_id="123")

docs.title: Migration Best Practices
docs.text:
• Always review auto-generated migrations
  • Use batch_alter_table for SQLite compatibility
  • Add indexes in separate migrations
  • Test migrations on copy of production data
  • Never modify applied migrations

docs.title: FreeStack Security Guide
docs.text: Security best practices for FreeStack applications.

docs.title: JWT Tokens
docs.text:
• Use strong secret keys (32+ bytes, randomly generated)
  • Rotate keys periodically
  • Use short access token lifetimes (15-30 minutes)
  • Use refresh tokens with longer lifetimes (7-30 days)
  • Implement token blacklisting for logout
  • Store tokens securely (HttpOnly cookies or secure storage)

docs.title: Password Security
docs.text:
• Enforce strong password policies (12+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols)
  • Use bcrypt with high cost factor (12+)
  • Never log passwords
  • Implement rate limiting on auth endpoints
  • Use constant-time comparison

docs.title: Session Management
docs.text:
• Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies
  • Short session timeouts
  • Rotate session IDs on privilege changes
  • Invalidate sessions on password change
  • Track concurrent sessions

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
• Implement per-user and per-IP limits
  • Use sliding window algorithm
  • Return standard headers (Retry-After, X-RateLimit-*)
  • Configure different limits for different endpoints

docs.title: Input Validation
docs.text:
• Validate all input with Pydantic models
  • Use allow-lists for enums
  • Sanitize user-generated content
  • Limit request sizes
  • Prevent mass assignment

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
• Restrict origins to known domains
  • Don't use wildcard with credentials
  • Set appropriate headers

docs.title: Security Headers
docs.text:
Always include: 

X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
X-Frame-Options: DENY
X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()

docs.title: Connection Security
docs.text:
• Use SSL/TLS for database connections
  • Use connection pooling
  • Limit database user permissions
  • Use separate users for app vs migrations

docs.title: Data Protection
docs.text:
• Encrypt sensitive fields at rest
  • Use parameterized queries (SQLAlchemy handles this)
  • Implement row-level security for multi-tenancy
  • Audit sensitive data access

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
• Review all migrations before applying
  • Test on staging data first
  • Have rollback procedures
  • Never modify applied migrations

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
• Private networks for internal services
  • Load balancers with WAF
  • Security groups / firewalls
  • VPC peering for cross-region

docs.title: Containers
docs.text:
• Run as non-root user
  • Read-only root filesystem
  • Drop unnecessary capabilities
  • Use distroless or minimal base images
  • Scan images for vulnerabilities

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• Never in code or config files
  • Use secret managers
  • Rotate regularly
  • Audit access

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
• Alert on failed auth attempts
  • Alert on unusual API patterns
  • Audit log aggregation
  • Intrusion detection

docs.title: OWASP Top 10 Mitigations
docs.text: Vulnerability Mitigation Broken Access Control RBAC, resource-level permissions, deny by default Cryptographic Failures TLS 1.3, strong ciphers, proper key management Injection Parameterized queries, input validation, ORM Insecure Design Threat modeling, security requirements, secure patterns Security Misconfiguration Hardened defaults, automated config checks Vulnerable Components Dependency scanning, automated updates, SBOM Identification/Authentication Failures MFA, rate limiting, secure session management Software/Data Integrity Failures Signed artifacts, CI/CD integrity, supply chain security Security Logging/Monitoring Failures Structured logging, centralized logs, alerting Server-Side Request Forgery URL validation, allow-lists, network segmentation
